commitResults.messageTitle: Level 7: save and load the task list
commitResults.messageBody:
Until now the task list existed only in memory, so closing the program
threw away everything the user had entered.

Add a Storage class that owns all file handling: it writes the list to
./data/goat.txt after every change and reads it back at start-up.
Keeping this in one class means the rest of Goat never has to know where
the data lives or how it is encoded.

Encoding is split the same way toString() already is. Task supplies the
shared "1 | description" half of a line, and each subclass prepends its
type letter and appends its own fields, so adding a task type later
means touching only that class. Decoding is centralised in
Storage.parseTask, which is the exact inverse. The done status is stored
as 1/0 rather than the X shown on screen, so the display wording can
change without invalidating files people have already saved.

Saving happens before the confirmation message is printed, so the user
is never told about a change that did not actually reach the disk.
Storage throws GoatException, which the existing catch around the
command dispatch already reports, so no new error handling was needed.

The app has to work on someone else's computer, so:
- the path is built with Paths.get("data", "goat.txt"), which is
  relative and lets Java insert whichever separator the running system
  uses, instead of baking in a "/" that would be wrong on Windows
- a missing file is not an error, since that is the normal state on a
  first run
- a missing ./data folder is created by Files.createDirectories
- a hand-edited file with a mistake in it names the offending line and
  starts with an empty list rather than crashing

Restore the text-ui-test harness and extend it to four runs of the
program: one that adds, marks and deletes; one that only lists, proving
the tasks came back from disk; one that reads a deliberately damaged
file; and one that starts with the save file deleted but the folder left
in place. The runner clears ./data first, because a leftover file would
be loaded at start-up and the test would stop being repeatable. Also
replace dos2unix with a tr fallback, as dos2unix is not installed on
macOS by default.

Ignore data/, since the saved list is personal to whoever runs the app,
and rename the remaining Duke references to Goat in README.md,
docs/README.md and AGENTS.md.
